text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.83% today, but this modest gain masks a sharp two-week decline of 8.4% that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has struggled as oil prices have weakened—Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August following comments from President Trump suggesting the Iran conflict would end "fairly soon," reducing geopolitical risk premium that typically supports energy prices. With US oil at $99.64 and global oil at $107.03, refiners and producers face lower margins and revenue outlooks than they did two weeks ago.

The earnings report coinciding with this shift in market sentiment appears to have triggered the initial leg down, and today's small rebound doesn't reverse the underlying pressure: if crude prices stabilize near current levels or drift lower on reduced geopolitical tension, integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips have less pricing power ahead.
